column1: # The workspace modules and what each may depend on. Every gate reads this
# file instead of naming modules itself, so adding a module is one row here
# and one member in moon.work (scripts/architecture_gate.mbtx checks that
# both agree). Rows are in dependency order: scripts/resolver_gate.mbtx stages
# them into its registry top to bottom.
# Columns, separated by one tab:
#   dir              the module directory, as moon.work lists it
#   name             the module name in its moon.mod
#   kind             four-target: every package builds and tests on wasm-gc,
#                    wasm, js and native with the same tests and public API;
#                    async tests are not allowed (wasm-gc skips them).
#                    runtime: the module runs on `targets` only; a package may
#                    narrow them with supported_targets in its moon.pkg.
#                    example: an unpublished executable at the module root,
#                    so `moon run <dir>` works. Built and tested on `targets`,
#                    but excluded from library coverage and release packaging.
#                    benchmark: an unpublished executable at the module root;
#                    built on `targets`, never run by gates, since timings
#                    depend on the host. Excluded from coverage and packaging.
#   targets          the targets the module's packages build on
#   module_deps      the modules its moon.mod may import (`-` for none)
#   package_imports  the packages its packages may import, besides its own:
#                    a prefix covers the package and the packages below it,
#                    `!prefix` denies them even when a broader prefix allows
#                    them, `*` allows anything
#   experimental     what its packages may list in
#                    options("allow-experimental-packages": [...]): an exact
#                    package name, a `prefix*` pattern, or `test:` before
#                    either for a package only the tests may import (`-` for
#                    none)
#   release          yes: a library in the coordinated release train; no:
#                    an unpublished harness or app. This is separate from
#                    kind so private modules keep their test/target rules
#                    and resolver coverage without becoming release candidates.
# An example or benchmark module may use anything: `*` in package_imports and
# experimental.
# Findings of the experimental opt-in probe on MoonBit 0.10.20 (the reasons
# behind the experimental column and the gates that read it):
# - A package that imports a package marked `experimental: true` lists it by
#   exact name: options("allow-experimental-packages": ["moonbitlang/core/async"]).
#   There are no patterns ("moonbitlang/core/async*" acknowledges nothing),
#   so each subpackage (async/fs, async/socket, ...) needs its own entry.
#   `true` acknowledges every experimental package; architecture_gate refuses it.
# - The same applies inside one module: importing an experimental package of
#   the module itself needs the entry too.
# - Imports for tests (`for "test"`) need the entry as well; `async test`
#   needs moonbitlang/core/async imported for "test". On wasm-gc async tests
#   are not run (0 tests), which is why four-target modules have none.
# - Only direct imports count: a package that imports a non-experimental
#   package built on core/async needs no entry.
# - A missing entry is a warning that --deny-warn does not turn into an
#   error, so scripts/runtime_gates.mbtx fails on the warning text itself.
# - .mbtx front matter accepts `import` and `permission` only, so a script
#   cannot acknowledge core/async: it runs, with the same warning on stderr.
#   scripts/gates.sh drops exactly that warning from script output.
